land.text: Byeonhan, which 'appears to be descended from the Jin state of southern Korea'

predecessors.note: Preceded by Jin (Korean state) on the Byeonhan infobox.

land.text: the Nakdong basin around Gimhae, where 'most Byeonhan states joined' the Gaya confederacy

successors.note: Gaya is split off from Cliopatria's Byeonhan row (-91..566) as a separate state; the Gaya dossier reviews the 534 and 561 shapes.

correction.text: the same shape, held for -91..300 only; from 301 the same land is the Gaya confederacy (the gaya dossier reviews it as gaya_301)

keyframe_review.note: -91..533 in Cliopatria (13,603 km2, 127.45-129.35E, 34.6-35.9N, the lower Nakdong and the south coast). Years change, not the outline. The page puts Byeonhan 'from around the beginning of the Common Era to the 4th century' and gives no area; its 13 listed statelets (Miryang, Haman, Goseong, Jinju/Sacheon, Seongju, Hadong/Namhae, Changwon, Gimcheon, Gimhae, Dongnae) reach Gimcheon and Seongju just north of the shape's 35.9N edge. The row's later shapes (534 and 561, 10,542 km2) are Gaya's after the loss of Gimhae, not Byeonhan's.

region.text: the twelve statelets of Byeonhan, 'present in the southern Korean peninsula' with Guya at Gimhae

ledger.note: 91 BCE: the Byeonhan confederacy of twelve statelets appears on the south coast. Cliopatria's first year; the infobox says 'Establishment: 194 BCE' but the lead says it 'existed from around the beginning of the Common Era to the 4th century', and the Samhan page that the Samhan formed around 108 BCE.

300: Byeonhan gives way to the Gaya confederacy. 'scholars have identified the late 3rd century as a period of transition from Byeonhan to Kaya'; the Byeonhan page says 'the decline of Byeonhan and the rise of the more centralized Gaya confederacy, which most Byeonhan states joined', infobox 'Transition to the Gaya confederacy: 42 CE', lead 'to the 4th century'. 300 is a bridge between those pages, not a page date.

wars.name: Eight Port Kingdoms War
wars.outcome: No territorial result on the pages; the Gaya page dates the war 'c. 209 - c. 212' between Silla and Kaya.
wars.note: The Gaya page dates the war '(c. 209 - c. 212)' between Silla and Kaya; the pages use the name Kaya for the Byeonhan states of the 3rd century, so the war falls in this dossier's life. The Silla page tells it differently: 'in the Eight Port Kingdoms War, Ara Gaya's prince asked Silla for a rescue army, and Silla intervened'. Moved here from the gaya dossier by the jk-02-a reviewer (it lay outside Gaya's life, 301-562).

certainty.note: A confederacy of twelve statelets with no frontier on any page; the Cliopatria outline is a block of the south coast.

sources.title: Byeonhan confederacy
sources.note: Identity, infobox (194 BCE, transition to Gaya 42 CE), lead (to the 4th century), the twelve statelets and their places, iron trade; no area.

sources.title: Gaya confederacy
sources.note: Transition from Byeonhan to Kaya in the late 3rd century; the confederacy's 42-532 'traditional period'.

sources.title: Samhan
sources.note: Samhan formed around 108 BCE; Byeonhan statelets 'later gave rise to the Kaya confederacy'.

notes: Cliopatria's Byeonhan row (-91..566, 657 years, three shapes) is two states: the Byeonhan confederacy and the Gaya confederacy that grew out of it (the 534 and 561 shapes match Silla's conquest of Geumgwan Gaya in 532 and Daegaya in 562, and Silla's own shape grows by 3,113 km2 in 534 while this one loses 3,061 km2). Split: this dossier keeps the years -91..300 and the shape byeonhan_-91; the new dossier gaya (cliopatria_names ['Byeonhan']) takes 301..562 and the 534 and 561 shapes. The validator therefore warns that byeonhan_534 and byeonhan_561 have no verdict here; that is intended. The split year is the weak point and sits at confidence 1: the pages give 42 CE (Byeonhan infobox; the Gaya 'traditional period' 42-532), 'the 2nd and 3rd centuries' (the confederacy formed), c. 209-212 (an Eight Port Kingdoms War 'between Silla and Kaya'), 'the late 3rd century' (scholars' transition) and 'the 4th century' (the Byeonhan lead); 300 was chosen to bridge the last two, and a reviewer who prefers the traditional 42 CE can move both dossiers. The Byeonhan page does not treat Byeonhan and Gaya as one entity: Gaya 'is described as a successor'. The Samhan infoboxes give 'Establishment: 194 BCE', contradicted by their own texts; Cliopatria's -91 is kept (see korean-jin notes). Capital: none; the twelve statelets had none, Guya (Gimhae) is only one of them. Page budget: 3 pages of 2 (Gaya and Samhan opened for the end).
